profile.campus: Time Warner Cable / Charter National Data Center West, Centennial CO (2 buildings, campus-level figures)
profile.address: 11011, East Peakview Avenue, Centennial, Arapahoe County, Colorado, 80111
profile.reading: This registry row is one of two buildings mapped under the name Time Warner Datacenter in Centennial, Colorado, roughly 110 meters apart, together forming what Time Warner Cable, now Charter Communications under the Spectrum brand, calls its National Data Center West campus. Trade press coverage from Data Center Dynamics, drawing on a Time Warner Cable announcement, documents an $85 million expansion of this campus that broke ground in June 2013, completed construction in late 2014, and came online in January 2015, bringing the site to a total of 170,000 square feet, 1,600 equipment racks, and 6.4 megawatts of critical IT load, a 75 percent capacity increase over the pre-expansion facility, as part of a $141 million total investment including earlier 2011 upgrades. The press coverage states the campus delivers digital video and IP based services for Time Warner Cable's core residential and business products, supporting roughly 70 million daily residential emails and billing for more than 15 million customers at the time, alongside WiFi, high speed data, voice, TV, and the company's IntelligentHome offering, and that the company pursued LEED Silver certification for the facility. A separate data center industry public records aggregator, datacenter.fyi, lists this same 11011 East Peakview Avenue address at 7.649 megawatts of total power capacity with 4.59 megawatts of IT load and a power usage effectiveness rating of approximately 1.67, connected to the Public Service Company of Colorado grid, a more granular current capacity figure than the original expansion announcement's 6.4 MW critical load figure. Charter Communications absorbed Time Warner Cable in a 2016 merger and operates the combined company's residential cable, internet, and phone services under the Spectrum consumer brand. Charter and Spectrum branded data centers supporting these operations, including this campus, are not typically marketed as public colocation facilities, unlike wholesale or retail colocation operators tracked elsewhere in this registry. These campus level figures apply to the two building National Data Center West campus as a whole rather than to this specific building alone, since no source found this session breaks capacity or square footage out by individual building.

reading.body:
No published power specification exists for this facility. The operator, Charter Communications, absorbed Time Warner Cable in 2016 and operates data centers supporting its Spectrum consumer cable and internet business, but does not appear to market these facilities with public technical specifications. Research attempts across multiple aggregator directories and Wikipedia sources found no published capacity figure.

Colorado has 17 mapped data center facilities, of which only 3 publish power capacity totaling 26.35 MW. This facility's ranking as fourth by published megawatts reflects the absence of a specification rather than a measured capacity; it carries no published figure and therefore contributes zero megawatts to the state total. The distinction matters for tracking: most mapped facilities in Colorado publish no capacity at all, making published figures sparse enough that a single unspecified site's ranking is a artifact of other sites' transparency rather than a measure of its size.

Whether this campus matters to AI scaling cannot be determined from available data. Operator specification pages are the only source used here for capacity claims, and this operator has not published one for this location. The site's actual power availability, grid interconnection status, and any commercial availability to AI workloads remain unknown.
